references.text: The fourth commandment, which states that one shall work for six days and rest on the seventh day, the Sabbath, which the Lord hallowed after creation.
The same command to work six days and rest on the seventh, emphasizing rest for both people and animals.
The Sabbath command is repeated with emphasis that work should be done in six days, and the seventh day is holy rest for the Lord.
Moses delivers the Sabbath command to the congregation of Israel, with a requirement to rest on the seventh day.
The Sabbath command in connection with the Lord's feasts, where work is forbidden on the seventh day.
Moses repeats the Sabbath command in his second law speech, with a requirement for six days of work and rest on the seventh.
Reference to working six days in connection with the celebration of the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
The basis for the Sabbath command: God completed His creation work in six days and rested on the seventh day.
The synagogue leader refers to the six working days as opposed to the Sabbath, which reflects this commandment.
Parallel between the weekly and seven-year Sabbath: God's requirement for rest applies regardless of the agricultural cycle.
Complements the weekly Sabbath with the seven-year Sabbath: God's requirement for rest applies to the entire rhythm of the earth.
